payload.summary:
While underway, the master of the tug boat observed 3
sampans around the barge and 3 perpetrators on the barge
taking scarp metals from the barge. About half an hour later,
the perpetrators were sighted left in the sampans. The tug
boat and barge continued their voyage and no assistance
was required. All crew members were accounted for and
without injury. Some scrap metals were stolen.
The master reported the incident to Singapore VTIS. Safety
broadcasts on anti-piracy watch were initiated to remind all
vessels to maintain vigilant watch at all times in the
Singapore Strait. Republic of Singapore Navy (RSN) and
Singapore Police Coast Guard (PCG) were notified of the
incident. Information of the incident was also shared with
Indonesian Authority.

payload.summary:
While at anchor, a crew member was confronted by six
perpetrators, reportedly armed with knives at Bay 02 on the
forward part of the ship. The crew was threatened, ordered
to remain silent and confined in the bosun store located
beneath the forward mooring station. The crew member
later freed himself and activated the fire alarm. The
perpetrators briefly returned but were unable to gain entry,
and subsequently escaped from the ship via the deck
leading overboard.
An immediate search was conducted onboard, with no
perpetrators found onboard. The crew was not injured.
Some unsecured items were stolen.
Subsequent investigation by ship crew revealed that the
padlock and securing arrangement of the bosun store door
had been tampered with, indicating forced entry. The stern
access to the engineer’s passageway was also found to
have been tampered with.
The incident was reported to local Coast Guard and
customs authorities.

payload.summary:
While at anchor, the crew noticed that several items,
namely cable wires and parts of the ship’s beam were
missing from the ship. The master subsequently confirmed
that no other losses or damages were sustained, and that
no further assistance was required. The crew were not
injured.
Upon receipt of the report, Coast Guard Station (CGS)
Manila immediately directed Coast Guard Sub-Station
(CGSS) Cavite City to conduct maritime patrol (MARPAT)
operations and establish contact with the ship. Thereafter,
all CGSS within the Cavite area were directed to conduct
shore patrols and maintain heightened vigilance, particularly
for possible sightings or recovery of the above-mentioned
items.

payload.summary:
While at anchor, the duty crew noted that the cover of the
hawse pipe of the starboard anchor was opened. After
informing the 2nd officer, the general alarm, including the
typhoon alarm was raised. A search was conducted with no
perpetrators found on board. Subsequently, the master
ordered an inventory and inspection of the deck equipment.
The crew were not injured. Some ship property/stores were
stolen.
The incident was reported to VTMS Corregidor and Coast
Guard Station (CGS) Manila. CGS Manila immediately
directed the duty MARPAT team to verify the incident, and
advised the Master to strengthen onboard security
measures and increase roving duties to prevent similar
incidents.

payload.summary:
Five robbers in a small wooden boat approached and
boarded the ship underway. They went into the engine room
and held the duty oiler hostage, threatening him with a gun
and a machete. They demanded to know the location of the
engine workshop and took the oiler's flashlight and phone.
The robbers told the oiler to stay in the workshop while they
searched for valuable items. When an engine alarm went
off, the oiler ran to the Engine Control Room, locked himself
in, and alerted the OOW. Alarm raised, public
announcement made, VTIS informed, and a distress
message broadcast. A Singapore navy vessel arrived and
conducted a search of the ship with the crew. No robbers
were found

were sighted in the steering gear room. The ship's general
alarm was activated and crew mustered. After conducting a
search onboard, master confirmed there was no further
sighting of the perpetrators and nothing was stolen. A crew

The RSN and SPCG were notified of the incident.

The SPCG boarded the ship at Eastern Boarding Ground
“B” (PEBGB) and conducted a search and investigation.

Yemen

051° 19.90' E
payload.summary:
Two suspicious boats carrying approximately six persons
each approached the vessel from the aft. The boats opened
continuous gunfire and ordered the vessel to stop.
The embarked armed security team responded immediately
and returned fire. An exchange of fire continued for
approximately 30 minutes, after which the suspected pirate
boats abandoned their approach and retreated from the
area.
During the incident, the Master activated the piracy alarm
and transmitted the Ship Security Alert System (SSAS).
Attempts were also made to contact nearby warships and
vessels to report the incident.
Following the event, all crew members and armed guards
were accounted for and found safe. No injuries, unauthorized
boarding, damage to the vessel, or damage to the cargo
have been reported. The vessel remains seaworthy and has
continued her voyage safely.

payload.summary:
Duty crew onboard a ship underway noticed a skiff with
armed pirates approaching. Seeing the threat, master
stopped the vessel, activated the distress alert, switched on
the AIS and instructed all crew to retreat to the citadel. After
a while, the crew exited the citadel. While no pirates were
seen, the crew noticed the boarding ladders still rigged to
the ship side resulting in the crew returning to the citadel as
precaution. The Master's assessment indicated that four
pirates had boarded the ship and later departed. All crew
reported safe.
